    Add a species with a country or region centroid to a geographic dataset

    add_species_centroid.Rd

    This function adds a single species record to an existing data frame of geographic occurrences. It uses the `countryref` dataset from the `CoordinateCleaner` package to obtain the centroid coordinates of a specified country or region.

    add_species_centroid(
  df,
  species_name,
  iso3,
  region = NULL,
  col_species = "species",
  col_lon = "lon",
  col_lat = "lat"
)

    Arguments

    df

    A data frame containing a species column, a latitude column and a longitude column.

    species_name

    Character. The species name to add.

    iso3

    Character. The ISO3 code of the country in which the species is present.

    region

    Character or NULL (default NULL). Optional region within the country (e.g., a province/state). If provided, the function will return the centroid of the region instead of the whole country.

    col_species

    Character. Name of the column in `df` for species names.

    col_lon

    Character. Name of the column in `df` for longitude values.

    col_lat

    Character. Name of the column in `df` for latitude values.

    Value

    A data frame with the new species row appended to the input `df`.

    Details

    This function was designed for when species are missing from a GBIF dataset and you want to provide a placeholder occurrence at a country/region centroid.

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Add Quercus sagrana in Cuba
df <- add_species_centroid(gbif_df,
                           "Quercus sagrana",
                           "CUB")
} # }
